clue.text: Fruit nomads gathered haphazardly

indicators.note: things gathered haphazardly are thrown together in no order, so the letters of nomads are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wandering herders pick fruit at random as they pass through.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark plum, a stone fruit often used for jam.

clue.text: Consider unimportant duke is superior to another noble

indicators.note: in a down clue, being superior to something means sitting above it, so the earlier pieces come first

parts.note: taken as written
a count is a nobleman, like the duke before it

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark that a duke outranks some other aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: To discount a suggestion is to disregard it as not worth taking seriously.

clue.text: Sounding catty, what makes your setter in debt to another?

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so this gives the word for oneself
someone in debt is owing money

explanation.surface: A riddle about the noise a cat makes and a setter who owes money.
explanation.definitionFit: Meowing is the mewing cry of a cat, so a meowing sound is literally cat-like.

clue.text: Circle, say, that includes appropriate clothing supplier

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: one word is said to include another when it holds it inside, so the outer word wraps the other

parts.note: to utter is to say aloud
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: A shop in a ring of buildings sells suitable clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or tradesman selling clothing and equipment, especially for a particular activity.

clue.text: Deterrents to improper conduct, namely regulations about parking

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for namely

indicators.note: one word goes about another when it surrounds it

parts.note: rules are regulations

explanation.surface: Parking rules are presented as the things that stop people behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruples are moral qualms or principles that hold a person back from doing wrong.

clue.text: In short, officer material, including our soldier perhaps — one of those upholding standards

indicators.note: the officer-and-material pair includes the next word inside it

parts.note: Col is the short form of colonel, an army officer
serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric used for uniforms
taken as written
a soldier ant is one caste of ant, so soldier is an example of an ant

explanation.surface: An officer's uniform cloth is said to include one of our own soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Standards here are regimental flags, the colours; this rank of sergeant in the British Army originally carried them in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour sergeant is a senior army NCO whose traditional duty was guarding the regimental colours, the flags carried as standards.

clue.text: Result that's surprising highly-placed clique

parts.note: up means high or raised
a set is a social circle or clique

explanation.surface: A shock outcome is blamed on a privileged in-crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an upset is an unexpected win by the underdog, an outcome nobody predicted.

clue.text: Practical joke, for example, turned up in Fifties

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the run of fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so several fifties give a run of that letter

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned over so it reads the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prank, for instance, that resurfaced in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-pull is a hoax or tease played on someone for fun, a mild trick.

clue.text: Notice article and become filled with anger

parts.note: to notice is to see
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Reading some newspaper piece makes someone furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, boiling with rage like a simmering pot.

clue.text: Deceptive behaviour as drunk fleeces parents

indicators.note: a drunk person is muddled, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An inebriated child swindles their mother and father.
explanation.definitionFit: False pretences are lies or misrepresentation used to get something, a classic form of fraud.

clue.text: Deficit resulting from one kind of movie season in US

parts.note: a short is a brief film
Americans call autumn the fall

explanation.surface: A cinema loses money on a certain type of film shown in American autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is the amount by which something falls short of what is needed, a deficit.

clue.text: Smooth changeover that's central for houseguests

indicators.note: the letters come from the middle of the word, so the answer lies inside it

parts.note: the answer sits in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A hotel boasts of seamless handovers that matter most to its visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A segue is an uninterrupted transition from one topic or piece of music to the next.

clue.text: First points for big win as all the leaders have quit

indicators.note: every word loses its leading letter, its leader having quit

explanation.surface: A sports commentary: the first points for a big win came when the team's leaders walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the leaders have quit' drops the opening letters of FOR, BIG, WIN and AS, leaving OR, IG, IN and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting points or sources from which things arise are what 'first points' describes.

clue.text: False statement taken out of account ruthlessly

indicators.note: the answer is lifted straight from within these words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A lie is ruthlessly deleted from a report of events.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth is a lie, something stated that is not true.

clue.text: Man on board announced time for retirement

indicators.note: said aloud the chess piece's name sounds like the answer, its silent first letter dropping out

parts.note: the knight is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A chess player declares it is time to quit the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is when people retire, meaning go to bed to sleep.

clue.text: Second family member entering college once, maybe

indicators.note: the pieces go into the college word

parts.note: a poly, or polytechnic, was a type of British college before they became universities in 1992
a sib is a sibling, a brother or sister

explanation.surface: A brother or sister briefly enrolled at a college that has since closed, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Possibly and maybe are synonyms, both expressing that something might be so.

clue.text: Restless rascal I confined within one part of camp

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
a means one

indicators.note: being confined within something means being shut inside it

parts.note: a tent is one unit of a campsite
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scamp grows fidgety after being shut inside a tent on a camping trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient means unable to wait calmly, fidgety and eager for things to move on.

clue.text: Those serving, with score in mind

parts.note: men are the troops serving in the forces
a tally is a running score or count

explanation.surface: Servicemen keep a count of points in their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentally means in or by the mind, done as a thought rather than physically.

clue.text: Be domineering and make too much of issue?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dominate or bully
second meaning, playful: to ... is to bear too much issue, that is to give birth to too many children

explanation.walkthrough: Issue means offspring, so the second half reads as having too many children.
explanation.definitionFit: Overbear means to overpower by force of will, and its parts suggest producing excessive offspring.

clue.text: Is it circular letter penned by empress who's away from home?

indicators.note: the pieces are penned, or shut in, by the empress's letters

parts.note: VR is Victoria Regina; Queen Victoria was also Empress of India
taken as written
taken as written
the round letter O

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks whether a round-robin letter was written by an empress.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone staying or calling at a place other than their own home.

clue.text: European included in step taken to produce truce

indicators.note: one piece is included in, so sits inside, the other

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A step taken with a European nation produces a ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace and a truce both mean an end to fighting, though a truce is usually temporary.

clue.text: University community installing Andrew, oddly, in top spot

indicators.note: the top spot installs, or holds within, the other piece

parts.note: the acme is the peak or highest point

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the name are taken

parts.note: taken as written; its first, third and fifth letters are kept

explanation.surface: A university installs someone named Andrew in its highest post.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic world, the community of scholars at universities.

clue.text: Not many supporting rogue measure restricting people's movements

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible scoundrel
few means not many

explanation.surface: Only a handful back a maverick policy to limit where people can go.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is an order requiring people to stay indoors during set hours.

clue.text: Revolting coach put another player in inferior position

definitions.text: put another player in inferior position

parts.note: people who are up are in revolt, as in up in arms
a stagecoach, or stage, is a horse-drawn coach

explanation.surface: A rebellious trainer sidelines one of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like disgusting but means rebelling here.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage an actor is to move upstage so they must face away from the audience, drawing attention from them.

clue.text: How to make pal paler, producing venomous creature

parts.note: the way to turn one word into a longer one is to add letters, so the instruction itself supplies add
taken as written; removing the shorter word from it leaves the letters that must be added
taken as written, the part of the longer word already present

explanation.surface: A friend going pale on meeting a poisonous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is a venomous viper, Britain's only poisonous snake.

clue.text: Remove person in crowd being filmed in front of court

indicators.note: the first piece stands in front of the second

parts.note: an extra is a film actor hired to fill a crowd scene

explanation.surface: A film extra is thrown out in front of a courthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to pull it out or take it away, as a dentist does a tooth.

clue.text: Thick edition that's bound

parts.note: fat means thick, as in a fat book

explanation.surface: A hefty book edition with a hard binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Fated and bound both mean destined, certain to happen, as in bound to fail.

clue.text: Fish has gone bad in angler's basket

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the basket

parts.note: a creel is a wicker basket for holding caught fish

indicators.note: something gone bad has changed for the worse, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be shuffled

explanation.surface: An angler finds the catch has rotted in their basket.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger eel is a large marine eel, a sea fish caught around Britain.

clue.text: Officer in charge of females inside fighting outfit

definitions.text: Officer in charge of females inside

parts.note: war is fighting
a dress is a garment or outfit

explanation.surface: An officer in charge of women wears combat uniform under it all.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside is slang for in prison, so the definition is a prison officer for female inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardress is a female prison warder, guarding women held in jail.

clue.text: It's very hard having fish in place of pork?

indicators.note: the fish goes inside the pig's home

parts.note: a sty is where pigs are kept, so it is home to pork on the hoof
the eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A cook finds it tough to swap fish for pork in a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard like steel, or unyielding and tough in character.
